Title: Fahmi acknowledges PKR delegates' concerns over government communication strategy
Article:
AYЕR KEROH: PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil has acknowledged concerns raised by party delegates over the government's communication strategy, particularly the difficulty in translating macroeconomic achievements into benefits felt at the household level.
Fahmi said the issue was among the key messages emerging midway through the 2026 PKR National Congress, with delegates calling for improvements to the party's machinery, as well as its communication and information strategies.
"There has been a lot of criticism and many matters that require reflection.
"We need to consider how to strengthen the party machinery, including making adjustments to our communication and information strategies," he told reporters at the Melaka International Trade Centre here today.
Fahmi, who is also communications minister, said the party leadership was taking the feedback seriously and was prepared to make changes.
He said Prime Minister and PKR president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, along with other party leaders, had adopted a humble approach by listening to delegates and recognising that any changes must begin with the leadership itself.
"Many have said that much of the government's efforts and achievements, particularly those of a macroeconomic nature, may not yet have been translated into benefits that can be felt at the household economic level.
"This is one of the major messages for me, both at the Communications Ministry and in my roles as PKR information chief and Pakatan Harapan communications director," he said.
Fahmi said he would address some of the concerns when winding up the debate tomorrow, including planned changes to improve the delivery of information and identify issues most keenly felt by the public.
He also welcomed proposals from PKR division chiefs to play a greater role as conduits of information between the grassroots and the federal administration.
Fahmi said while such channels already existed, a more formal mechanism might be needed to ensure issues at the parliamentary constituency level could be effectively relayed to Putrajaya and followed up with solutions.

Title: Flores earthquake: No Malaysians affected, says embassy
Article:
JAKARTA: No Malaysians have been reported affected by the magnitude 7.7 earthquake that struck Flores in Indonesia's East Nusa Tenggara (NTT) province early Saturday.
The Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta said it had contacted Malaysians in NTT who were registered with the embassy, as well as Malaysian tourists who had informed the embassy of their whereabouts in the region.
"The Embassy is also in close contact with the Indonesian Foreign Affairs Ministry to get the latest situation update and, as of noon local time, there have been no reports of incidents involving Malaysian nationals," the embassy said in a statement.
Malaysians affected by the earthquake and requiring consular assistance can contact the Malaysian Embassy in Jakarta at +62 813 8081 3036 or email mwjakarta@kln.gov.my.
The embassy also expressed its sympathy to those affected and hoped that the authorities' efforts to manage the situation on the ground would proceed smoothly.
The earthquake struck at 4.58am local time, with its epicentre in the sea about 30km from Mbay at a depth of 15km.
It also triggered a tsunami warning, which the Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency lifted at 7.31am after monitoring showed no further significant rise in sea levels.
The National Disaster Management Agency said about 2,000 residents had been evacuated or had fled to safety following the earthquake that struck Flores Island.
Earlier, the Maumere Search and Rescue Office reported that the death toll from the earthquake and several strong aftershocks had risen to 20, with six people injured and two others still trapped.

Title: KDM withdraws support for GRS, says Priscella
Article:
PAPAR: Parti Kesejahteraan Demokratik Masyarakat (KDM) has decided to withdraw its support for the Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) government and move outside the administration ahead of the next state and general elections.
KDM president Priscella Peter said the decision was made unanimously by the party's supreme council, taking into account the party's interests and the need to rebuild public confidence at the grassroots.
She said the decision was not easy but necessary to give the party a clear direction and demonstrate that KDM was committed to engaging with voters beyond election periods.
"The important thing is that, in preparation for the state election and GE16, KDM and its supreme council have decided to move forward without being part of the GRS government.
"This is a difficult decision, but what matters is showing the people and our grassroots members that we have a clear direction," she told a press conference after the KDM briefing and direction-setting session ahead of GE16 at Beringgis Resort here today.
Priscella said developments following the previous election had affected the party and were among the factors behind its decision to move outside the GRS government.
She said KDM needed to rebuild public confidence before the next election instead of only taking action when Parliament or the state assembly was dissolved.
She added that KDM would not contest GE16 alone, but was open to working with other local parties to form a political bloc based on Sabah's interests.
"With Warisan, perhaps yes. With Star, yes. But we have not made a final decision as further discussions are needed.
"We are more inclined towards working with local parties," she said.
Priscella said the proposed Borneo Bloc would require further discussions with KDM's supreme council before it could be finalised.
She said discussions with other parties, including Parti Warisan and Parti Solidariti Tanah Airku (STAR), remained informal.
On KDM leaders holding positions in government agencies or government-linked companies (GLCs), she said the party would comply with the relevant protocols following its withdrawal of support for GRS.
"If the protocol states that they have to relinquish their positions, then that is what will happen," she said.
On reports that KDM deputy president Datuk Wetrom Bahanda would join Barisan Nasional, Priscella said the party had yet to receive any official letter or notification from him.
She said Wetrom, who is also the Kota Marudu MP, remained KDM deputy president.
"At this point, the party has not received any official letter or notification. He is still the party's deputy president," she said.
Priscella said Wetrom's attendance at events linked to other parties did not necessarily mean he had decided to leave KDM.
She said the decision to withdraw support for GRS was made by the party's supreme council and that she believed Wetrom was aware of it.
"His status remains as KDM deputy president," she said.
Media reports previously quoted BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi as indicating that Wetrom and his brother, Kudat MP Datuk Verdon Bahanda, were set to join BN, sparking speculation over Wetrom's position in KDM.

Title: AUKU abolition must involve students, academics, civil society, says youth NGO
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Youth-based non-governmental organisation Mandiri has called for broader stakeholder participation in the special committee coordinating the abolition of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU).
Its coordinator, Hamdin Nordin, said the Higher Education Ministry should also ensure wider stakeholder participation in drafting a new legal framework for the governance of higher education institutions.
He said the government's announcement to abolish AUKU was an important step towards strengthening democracy and freedom in higher education institutions.
"However, the announcement must be followed by a clear implementation process and timeline.
"The commitment should not become another reform promise that is announced but ultimately left unfinished.
"As such, we urge the ministry to publicly release an implementation plan and timeline, including the consultation process, preparation of the draft legislation, tabling in Parliament and the date the abolition will take effect," he said in a statement today.
Hamdin said the ministry should ensure the new legislation was drafted inclusively, with the participation of students, academics and civil society.
He said the ministry should also ensure the new legal framework did not reintroduce restrictions on student freedom in a different form or through other mechanisms.
"The abolition of AUKU must be in line with its original spirit, namely restoring student autonomy in managing student affairs and upholding academic freedom both within and outside campus," he said.
Hamdin said Mandiri would also continue supporting the student movement's campaign against AUKU, describing it as another "draconian" law that restricted students and should be abolished.
Earlier today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government would
abolish the Act as part
of its broader reform agenda, particularly in response to concerns raised by university students.
He said several amendments had already been made to give students greater freedom, but acknowledged that some remained dissatisfied and had submitted a memorandum calling for further changes.

Title: 10 Lojing vegetable farming firms issued DOE notices over EIA breaches
Article:
GUA MUSANG: The Kelantan Department of Environment (DOE) has issued notices to 10 vegetable farming companies in Lojing Highlands for violating environmental requirements.
The notices were issued under Sections 31 and 37 of the Environmental Quality Act 1974 for breaches of conditions imposed under approved Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs), including land clearance and planting activities.
Kelantan DOE deputy director Mohamad Zamzani Ibrahim told the New Straits Times that enforcement operations were conducted by officers from the Gua Musang branch throughout last year and from January to July this year following complaints from the public.
"DOE officers inspected vegetable farms in Lojing Highlands, and 10 operators who failed to comply with conditions imposed under their approved EIAs were issued notices under Sections 31 and 37 of the Environmental Quality Act 1974.
"Of the 10 companies, one was taken to court for failing to comply with the notice," he said.
Zamzani said several operators had expanded their vegetable farming activities to include crops such as tomatoes and long beans without complying with requirements related to land clearance and planting.
"They were found to have failed to adhere to EIA guidelines, including proper farm management practices such as appropriate waste disposal.
"Failure to properly manage farming activities could contribute to soil erosion and other environmental problems, which may affect nearby rivers," he said.
Zamzani said the Gua Musang DOE also issued 10 written field directives during the same period for minor offences or shortcomings that could be rectified immediately.
"Field directives are written instructions issued by our officers at the site during inspections.
"They involve minor offences or shortcomings that can be corrected immediately.
"If the instructions are not complied with, stronger enforcement action will be taken, including the issuance of a formal notice," he said.
He said formal notices were issued for more serious offences, particularly breaches of conditions under approved EIA requirements.
"Such notices are normally issued by the state director or branch chief, requiring project operators to take corrective measures within the stipulated period.
"If the notice is not complied with, an investigation paper will be opened for further legal action," he said.
On the single court action, Zamzani said it involved a company that failed to comply with a DOE notice, adding that the case would be brought to court this year.
He said enforcement measures were aimed at ensuring project operators, particularly those involved in agricultural activities, complied with EIA conditions and adopted proper environmental management practices.
He added that the state DOE would continue to monitor activities in Lojing Highlands and take enforcement action against operators found to have breached environmental regulations.

Title: India envoy urges Malaysian Indians to preserve roots
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Indians in Malaysia have been urged to uphold their cultural roots while contributing to the country they call home and strengthening longstanding ties between India and Malaysia.
India's Charge d'Affaires to Malaysia, Shri Hitesh Rajpal, said the Indian community, including professionals, students, workers, entrepreneurs, families and elders, remained an integral part of the larger Indian family.
He urged them to uphold hard work, integrity, mutual respect and harmony while preserving their language, culture and traditions.
"Please stay connected to your roots, nurture the language, culture and traditions you carry, and at the same time be exemplary citizens and residents who strengthen the warm friendship between India and Malaysia," he said at the High Commission of India's 80th Independence Day celebration today.
Rajpal said the community could support India's Viksit Bharat vision through knowledge, enterprise, skills and community service, helping the country realise its full potential by 2047.
He also called for stronger people-to-people ties, greater economic cooperation and mutual support between India and Malaysia.
He said bilateral ties had gained greater strategic depth, with cooperation expanding in areas including semiconductors, digital payments and fintech, security and counter-terrorism, healthcare, renewable energy, and technical and vocational education.
The relationship was elevated to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2024 during Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's state visit to India and further consolidated during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's official visit to Malaysia in February.
Rajpal said bilateral trade remained robust, with Malaysia ranking as India's third-largest trading partner in Asean, while defence and security ties continued to grow through military exchanges and joint exercises.
He said people-to-people ties remained a key pillar of bilateral relations, supported by tourism, education, cultural exchanges and the presence of nearly 2.75 million people of Indian origin in Malaysia.
The High Commission's Independence Day activities included a flag-hoisting ceremony at India House, the Bharat Ko Janiye quiz, the "India Through My Lens" photography competition and the #MyIndiaMyStory campaign.

Title: Subang Airport runway reopens after temporary closure following helicopter fire
Article:
SUBANG: The runway at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport here, which was temporarily closed following a helicopter fire earlier today, has reopened.
Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) chief executive officer Captain Datuk Norazman Mahmud said the runway was reopened following the incident at Taxiway Victor.
"The runway was opened for air traffic at the airport at 2.57pm. Passengers are advised to check with their respective airlines for the latest updates on their flights," he said when contacted.
He said eight inbound flights were diverted while another three flights had to delay their departure during
the temporary closure
.
Meanwhile, checks by the New Straits Times at the airport terminal's flight information board showed that most flights had been retimed.
CAAM earlier said the airport's runway had been closed, with all flights put on hold until further notice.
The closure followed an incident involving a Kamov Ka-32S helicopter, which caught fire at 12.28pm while undergoing an engine ground run as part of maintenance activities.
Four Ukrainian men
, including a pilot, co-pilot and two crew members, were involved in the incident, with one sustaining minor injuries after being struck by debris.

Title: Defence Capacity Blueprint 2026–2030: Building Malaysia's defence beyond military assets
Article:
LETTERS:
When discussions turn to national defence, public attention is often drawn to visible military capabilities such as fighter jets, naval vessels, tanks and advanced weapon systems.
These assets are, without a doubt, indispensable for safeguarding national sovereignty.
However, in today's increasingly complex security environment, military hardware alone can no longer determine a country's defence readiness.
The true measure of defence capability lies equally in the strength of its people, institutions, technology capacity and national resilience. This broader understanding of defence is what underpins Malaysia's Defence Capacity Blueprint (RTKP) 2026 – 2030.
The current conflict in Europe and the Middle East, as well as changes of countries' approaches towards the South China Sea, have shown there is a definite change in the world strategic environment.
The 2025 Mid-Term Review of the Defence White Paper has recognised that Malaysia is now living in an increasingly complex security landscape, shaped by the geopolitical landscape, hybrid warfare, technological advances and climate-related challenges.
These threats are not new, but they are becoming more interconnected and complex, requiring defence institutions to respond effectively. Against this backdrop, RTKP represents Malaysia's strategic investment in the pillars that will determine defence effectiveness over the coming decade.
The first of these pillars is the people. Though defence capability is regularly connected with military platforms, its effectiveness ultimately depends on the people operating them, the leaders making critical decisions, and the institutions sustaining them.
The blueprint recognises that strengthening professional military education through continuous learning, leadership development, institutional learning, and workforce sustainability ensures that defence personnel possess not only operational competence but also the adaptability and critical thinking needed to respond to an increasingly complex security challenge.
In this sense, the blueprint recognises that people remain the decisive factor in national defence.
However, building defence capacity extends beyond developing capable defence professionals. The adoption of the Whole of Government and Whole of Society (WOGOS) approach reflects the understanding that modern security challenges, including cyber-attacks, disinformation, supply chain disruptions and climate-related emergencies, transcend traditional military boundaries.
Through the concept of Total Defence (HANRUH), the blueprint promotes a shared responsibility towards safeguarding national security by strengthening public awareness, fostering strategic partnerships and enhancing societal resilience.
In this way, it evolves from a military function into a shared national responsibility.
Innovation is the third pillar of this transformation. As emerging technologies reshape the character of conflict, sustaining defence capability will increasingly depend on scientific expertise, technological innovation and a competitive defence industry.
Therefore, the blueprint seeks to strengthen collaboration between government and academia and will help ensure that Malaysia possesses not only modern defence systems, but also the knowledge and expertise needed to support them over the long term.
In the end, the true strength of a nation's defence is measured not only via military assets that it possesses, but by the national capacity it builds to sustain them. In this regard, the blueprint provides Malaysia with a strategic framework to strengthen that capacity and prepare the nation for the uncertainties of tomorrow's security environment.
Rear Admiral Datuk Yusne Mokhtar
Malaysian Institute of Defence and Security (MiDAS)

Title: Tourism Ministry cracks down on unlicensed operators in KL
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Tourism, Arts and Culture Ministry issued 15 inspection notices for various offences under the Tourism Industry Act 1992 during a two-day enforcement operation around Kuala Lumpur that began on Wednesday.
In a statement today, the ministry said nine of the notices were issued under Subsection 5(2) for operating a tourism business without a valid licence.
"Three tourist locations, nine business premises and three people were inspected over the course of the operation.
"Intelligence work in collaboration with the Kuala Lumpur Tourist Guide Association (KLTGA) was also carried out to detect individuals suspected of carrying out tourist guide activities without valid licences.
"Enforcement action under Subsection 21(1) was taken against those found doing so."
The ministry said the operation also flagged other violations, including using private or unlicensed vehicles to ferry tourists, breaching licence conditions and doing business with unlicensed operators.
Private or unlicensed vehicles identified being used for tourist transport will be dealt with by the Land Public Transport Agency and Road Transport Department.
"Further investigations will be conducted before legal action is taken against individuals, entities, owners and other relevant parties involved," it said.
The ministry warned unlicensed parties not to offer tourism services.
"The public and industry players are encouraged to channel any information on tourism activities suspected of violating laws and regulations through the Public Complaints Management System at the following link: https://motac.spab.gov.my/eApps/system/index.do," it said.

Title: Tawau drone medicine pilot identifies two landing sites
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Health Ministry and Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) are preparing a pilot medication-drone delivery service in Tawau, with the launch and landing sites identified.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the launch site had been identified at Tawau Health Clinic, while landing sites had been identified at MCMC's National Information Dissemination Centre (Nadi) centres in Sungai Imam and Tinagat.
"The Digital Health Division (BKD), in collaboration with the Pharmacy Programme, will conduct a workshop and training on procedures or SOPs involving healthcare personnel at the Tawau Health Clinic and the Nadi centres," he said during a press conference after the Ministry of Health Training Institutes (ILKKM) convocation ceremony at Universiti Malaysia Sabah here.
Dzulkefly said the ministry and MCMC had also appointed Alpha Catalyst as the official evaluator for the pilot project to assess the effectiveness of the initiative.
"If everything is in place for the pilot project, an official launch ceremony to be jointly organised by the Health Ministry and the Ministry of Communications will be held in September or October this year," he said.

Title: Hospital director transferred over sexual harassment probe, says Dzulkefly
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: The Health Ministry has taken administrative action against a hospital director in Sabah following an internal investigation into an alleged sexual harassment case.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the former director had been transferred to the Sabah Health Department as a medical officer, pending further action.
"Administratively, the ministry has completed the internal investigation. Among the actions taken was the transfer of the director to a medical officer's position in the medical division of the Sabah Health Department.
"The victim has also been given full support and psychiatric treatment, and has returned to a better working environment," he said during a press conference after the ministry's Training Institutes convocation at Universiti Malaysia Sabah here.
Last month, the issue was raised by Kapayan assemblyman Chin Teck Ming and Sabah Warisan Health Bureau chief Dr Istefan Koh
over the alleged wrongdoings
.
Sabah police commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun also acknowledged that a police report was lodged earlier this year.
"The official report from the department has been submitted to Public Service Department, based on the officer's grade, as it has its own jurisdiction and authority to handle this matter," Dzulkefly said.
On mental health, especially involving students in schools, Dzulkefly said no single ministry could address various health and public health challenges alone.
He said the National Centre of Excellence for Mental Health (NCEM) had been engaging with the Education Ministry on mental health challenges among school students.
"The Education Ministry recognises the commitment of NCEM in addressing these issues responsively and immediately, including identifying early trends and signs, especially among adolescents and minors.
"This is a vulnerable or high-risk group that we need to pay attention to," he said.
Dzulkefly said discussions focused on immediate preparedness and mobilising a fast response to mental health issues among vulnerable groups.

Title: Seven hotspots detected in Malaysia as haze worsens in Sarawak
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of seven hotspots were detected in the country, with five in Sarawak and two in Sabah, as air quality deteriorated in several areas of Sarawak, which recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings.
Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said that, based on the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) report dated Aug 14, a total of 226 hotspots were also detected in Kalimantan, while another five were recorded in Sumatra.
As of 11am today, nine areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy API readings, with Kuching recording the highest at 164, followed by Samarahan (161), Serian IPD (160), Bintulu and Sarikei (157), Sri Aman (153), Sibu (152), Mukah (151), and Samalaju (118).
"The deterioration in air quality was caused by the movement of haze from various directions, including moderate to dense transboundary smoke plumes from clusters of hotspots in West Kalimantan moving northwards into the western part of the state.
"Moderate to dense localised smoke plumes were also observed, originating from hotspots in large parts of Kalimantan, central Sarawak, and central Sumatra," she said in a statement today.
She said several air quality monitoring stations in West Kalimantan as well as western and central Sarawak also recorded unhealthy readings.
However, ASMC said the full extent of the hotspot and haze situation in the region could not be determined due to cloud cover.
In view of the situation, Azuri Azizah said the DOE had stepped up enforcement action and daily patrols in areas prone to open burning, in addition to monitoring API readings from time to time.
"The National Open Burning Action Plan and National Haze Action Plan have also been activated to coordinate the actions of government agencies in addressing open burning and haze situations," she said.
She advised landowners to monitor areas prone to and frequently affected by fires, including landfill sites, forests, peatlands, plantations, agricultural, and industrial areas, and to take measures to prevent intrusion by irresponsible parties.
The public was also reminded not to carry out open burning and to report any cases of open burning or fires to the Fire and Rescue Department at 999 or the DOE toll-free line at 1-800-88-2727.

Title: Explainer: What abolishing AUKU means for universities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has announced that the government will abolish the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU).
Originally introduced to regulate the establishment and administration of public universities, AUKU later became associated with restrictions on student activism and political activities on campuses, particularly following amendments in the mid-1970s.
WHAT IS AUKU?
The Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (Act 30) was enacted to provide the legal framework for the establishment, governance and administration of public universities and university colleges in Malaysia.
It came into force on April 30, 1971, replacing the Emergency (Essential Powers) Ordinance No. 74, 1971, and remains the primary law governing public higher education institutions.
HOW AUKU EVOLVED
1971:
Parliament passed AUKU to establish a comprehensive legal framework for public universities, covering governance, administration, finances and the powers of university authorities.
The original Act primarily focused on institutional management rather than student political activities.
1975:
Parliament passed amendments that significantly expanded the government's oversight of public universities.
Among the key changes was greater government authority over university governance, including the appointment of vice-chancellors, who in turn appointed deans, deputy deans and heads of schools and institutes, replacing the previous practice of elections among academics.
1996:
Further amendments restructured the governance of public universities as part of efforts to corporatise the higher education sector. The changes included reducing the size of university senates and governing councils to streamline institutional management.
2009 and 2012
: Following years of debate over university autonomy and the competitiveness of Malaysia's higher education sector, Parliament introduced amendments that relaxed some restrictions on students.
The reforms shifted certain disciplinary and administrative powers over students from the Education Minister to university authorities, while the 2012 amendments also allowed students to join political parties.
2018:
The Pakatan Harapan administration repealed Section 15(2)(c), removing the prohibition on students participating in political activities organised by political parties within university campuses. The move paved the way for greater student political participation.
2024:
Parliament approved further amendments to strengthen student representative councils by allowing them to collect and manage funds in their own name.
The amendments also shifted student disciplinary authority from the vice-chancellor to a Student Disciplinary Committee, while updating provisions relating to student representative councils and university administration.
WHY HAS AUKU BEEN CONTROVERSIAL?
Despite the repeal of Section 15(2)(c), several student organisations continued to call for further reforms to AUKU, arguing that the Act still empowers vice-chancellors to suspend or dissolve student groups deemed to have acted in a manner prejudicial to the interests or harmony of the university.
WHAT HAPPENS NEXT?
Following the announcement, Anwar said the government's proposal to abolish AUKU would be tabled at the Cabinet meeting on Wednesday.
This would mark a major change to Malaysia's higher education legislation, which has been in force since 1971.

Title: 2027 Budget to focus on expanding AI adoption, says Gobind
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will focus on expanding the use of artificial intelligence (AI), including exploring systems to promote wider access to AI tools, in the 2027 Budget to be tabled in October.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said AI Malaysia, launched three weeks ago by the Digital Ministry, would require significant funding to mobilise expertise and develop AI infrastructure to support its adoption across sectors.
"Beyond experts, we also need to build AI infrastructure that can support every sector in Malaysia and drive the technology forward.
"So, I will focus on this in the 2027 Budget to be tabled in October," he told reporters after delivering a speech at the Petaling Jaya (PJ) Startup Festival 2026 today.
Gobind said the initiative was important to ensure the benefits of AI could be widely accessible, particularly as high costs could limit its adoption.
He said while businesses and the public were increasingly aware of AI's benefits, the cost of using the technology remained a barrier to wider adoption.
"We need to look at how technology can help small traders, particularly micro, small and medium enterprises. This is something I will also focus on.
"But it is still too early to discuss the details. Hopefully, when Budget 2027 is tabled, we will hear about initiatives that can help," he said.
Gobind said the PJ Startup Festival, an annual event, features about 100 booths this year and is expected to attract around 2,000 participants, including members of the public.
The Damansara MP said the festival reflected growing attention on startups and efforts to strengthen the country's startup ecosystem.
He added that the event also provided a platform to identify new talent and potential, while creating opportunities for investors to discover and support innovative businesses and ideas.

Title: 'That's my wife and son': Husband's fears confirmed after tanker crash
Article:
TEMERLOH: "That is my wife and son," were the words that flashed through Saifulnizam Sulaiman's mind after learning of a horrific crash involving a car and a
fuel tanker lorry
at Km9 of Jalan Temerloh-Triang near Kampung Lebak yesterday.
Saifulnizam, 39, said his wife Nur Fatima Syuhada Abdullah, 39, and their son Muhamad Fattah Aisy, 12, were travelling from Jerantut to Seremban, Negri Sembilan, when the crash occurred.
He said he learned of the incident through social media and immediately felt the victims were his wife and son.
"I knew they were on their way to Seremban to meet me.
"As soon as I saw the viral video, I tried calling my wife, but failed. My messages were also unanswered, and at that point, I suspected the victims were my wife and child.
"I immediately contacted my family in Pahang to get confirmation," he said when met at the Forensic Unit of Sultan Ahmad Shah Hospital here today.
[[nid:1511683]]
In the
4pm incident
, a tanker carrying 32,000 litres of fuel from Bera to Temerloh lost control, overturned, and crushed the car occupied by the mother and son.
The crash resulted in both victims being burnt to death, while the 37-year-old tanker driver sustained minor injuries.
Saifulnizam said he was in Seremban for work at the time, while his wife had left Jerantut after their son finished school yesterday.
He said they left Jerantut at about 2pm and were expected to arrive in Seremban at 6pm.
He added that he felt uneasy when messages sent to his wife at about 5pm went unanswered.
"I rushed to Temerloh to get confirmation, and I have seen and hugged the bodies of my wife and son at the forensic unit.
"My priority now is to handle their funeral arrangements as quickly as possible," he said.
Meanwhile, Temerloh district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron said the tanker driver involved in the crash had been remanded for four days starting today.
He said the man was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for dangerous driving causing death.
He added that although the family had provided statements to the police, official identity confirmation would be carried out through deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) testing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tengku Mahkota Pahang makes history as first royal to complete RMAF helicopter course
Article:
ALOR STAR: Tengku Mahkota Pahang Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah created history as the first royal family member to complete the Basic Helicopter Flying Course Series 67 (A)/26 at the Air Force College (KTU) here.
He underwent the course from June 2 to July 31 using an EC120B Colibri helicopter.
Tengku Hassanal was among 39 participants who completed flight training and received their Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) Flying Wings.
The presentation of the wings was performed by the Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, as RMAF Colonel-in-Chief, during a parade ceremony at the KTU parade ground today.
The 39 graduates comprised 38 young pilots and two fighter weapon sensor officers from all three branches of the armed forces.
Of the total, 32 officers were from the RMAF, while three were from the army and four were from the Royal Malaysian Navy.
The ceremony involved graduates from four flight courses, namely the Basic Helicopter Flying Course Series 67(A)/26, Basic Helicopter Flying Course Series 67/25, Basic Flying Course Series 87/25, and Fighter Weapon Sensor Officer Basic Course Series 01/25.
Six awards were presented to top graduates based on achievements in flying, academics, discipline, and leadership during the ceremony.
The Overall Best Rotary Wing Graduate award was presented to Lieutenant Ahmad Faiz Roslan, who received the Air Force Chief Trophy, while the Overall Best Fixed Wing Graduate went to Lieutenant Safwan Lukman Miswanto, who received the Air Force Chief Trophy.
Meanwhile, the Overall Best Fighter Weapon Sensor Officer Graduate was awarded to Lieutenant Muhamad Syahmi Mohd Nawi, who received the Air Education and Training Commander Trophy.
Also receiving recognition were Best Academic Graduate Lieutenant Muhammad Naim Rami, who received the Air Education and Training Commander Trophy, and Best Rotary Wing Graduate Lieutenant Ku Muhammad Azfar Ku Abdul Shukur, who received the Commandant Trophy.
The Best Fixed Wing Graduate was awarded to Lieutenant Muhammad Atif Muhamad Noor Azam, who received the Commandant Trophy.
RMAF chief General Tan Sri Muhamad Norazlan Aris said the success of the Tengku Mahkota Pahang and all graduates resulted from perseverance, fighting spirit, mental resilience, and high discipline throughout training.
He said the achievement was supported by prayers, encouragement, and motivation from parents and family members who stood behind the graduates throughout the training period.
"The conferment of flying wings is not the end of a journey. Instead, it marks the beginning of a much greater trust and responsibility.
"From today, the wings pinned to your chests carry the dignity, hopes, and trust of the service and nation," he said.
Norazlan said every wings recipient is required to uphold discipline, integrity, courage, and loyalty in fulfilling their trust and defending the sovereignty of the nation's airspace.
He said the knowledge, capabilities, and personal character instilled during training will enable graduates to carry out their assigned duties with full dedication for religion, race, and country.

Title: Ukrainian crew member injured by debris in Subang helicopter fire
Article:
SUBANG: A Ukrainian crew member was lightly injured after being struck by debris when a helicopter caught fire at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport here today.
The victim was among four Ukrainian men on board, including a pilot, co-pilot, and two crew members, involved in the incident.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said information from the Airport Fire and Rescue Service indicated the injured man was outside the helicopter when he was hit by flying debris.
Ashrul earlier said
four people escaped
the aircraft after it caught fire while preparing to take off for an engine test following repairs.
Firefighters from the Airport Fire and Rescue Service and the Bukit Jelutong Fire and Rescue Station were deployed to the scene.

Title: PKR delegates question Umno sincerity and loyalty as Unity Government partner
Article:
AYER KEROH: Umno came under criticism from PKR delegates at the party's 2026 National Congress today, with some questioning its sincerity and loyalty as a partner in the Unity Government and accusing it of "stabbing PKR in the back".
Several delegates raised concerns over PKR's cooperation with Umno and Barisan Nasional (BN) through Pakatan Harapan (PH), claiming that the partnership at the federal level had not translated into electoral cooperation, particularly in the Johor and Negri Sembilan state elections.
Selangor PKR delegate Danish Hairudin said the two polls had exposed what he described as Umno's lack of sincerity and solidarity, despite both parties being part of the Unity Government.
He said political cooperation, while necessary for stability, should not come at the expense of PKR's interests or dignity.
"We accepted them as partners because the country needed stability, but political friendship must have limits and dignity.
"We cannot shake hands in Putrajaya while, on the political battlefield, the same hand stabs us in the back," he said when debating the president's policy speech.
Danish, who is also PKR Youth information chief, claimed Umno's lack of loyalty was evident in the Johor and Negri Sembilan state elections, despite both parties being partners at the federal level.
"In Johor, Umno stabbed us. In Negri Sembilan, Umno beheaded us, even though we were living under the same roof. Are we still going to remain silent?" he said.
He said the grassroots wanted the PKR leadership to be given the mandate to make firmer political decisions, allowing the party and its machinery to move forward.
Danish said PKR had never demanded that Umno bow to it or abandon its political identity, but stressed that cooperation must be built on sincerity and mutual respect.
"We have been too busy looking after the feelings of others that we have forgotten to look after our own family.
"Let this congress send a clear message: those who are loyal, we appreciate; those who are friends, we respect; but those who attack us, we will fight — just as we have fought over the past 20 years," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fuel tanker driver remanded over crash that killed mother and son in Temerloh
Article:
TEMERLOH: The fuel tanker driver involved in a fatal crash that claimed the lives of a mother and her son at Km9 of Jalan Temerloh-Triang near Kampung Lebak yesterday has been remanded for four days to assist in investigations.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Nasyim Bahron said the 37-year-old man was remanded from today until Tuesday.
He said the driver was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for dangerous driving causing death.
"Urine screening tests conducted on the driver returned negative for drugs," he said in a statement.
In the 4pm incident yesterday, a woman and her son were burnt to death after their
car was crushed by a tanker
carrying 32,000 litres of diesel and petrol.
The crash caused both the tanker and the car to catch fire, trapping the two victims inside. The tanker driver sustained minor injuries.
The incident occurred while the mother and son were travelling from Jerantut to Seremban, Negri Sembilan.
Initial police investigations revealed that the crash occurred after the tanker, which was travelling from Seremban to Temerloh, lost control, overturned, and crushed the victims' car.
Nasyim said post-mortem examinations on the two bodies were conducted at the Sultan Ahmad Shah Hospital here today.
He said burial arrangements might be delayed until deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) test results were obtained.
However, he said next-of-kin had come forward to identify the victims as Nur Fatima Abdullah, 39, and her son, Muhamad Fattah Aisy Nuafal Saifulnizam, 12, from Jerantut.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Phase 3 STR cash aid payout begins today for 5.3 million recipients
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Finance Ministry will disburse Phase 3 payments of the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) cash aid in stages starting today to 5.3 million recipients, involving an allocation of RM1.2 billion.
The number of recipients has grown by 300,000 since the start of the year, when it stood at five million, comprising 3.9 million low- and middle-income households and 1.4 million single senior citizens.
"Phase 3 payments range from RM150 to RM600 depending on income and number of children, while single senior citizens will receive RM150.
"Overall, the total disbursement for the first three phases of 2026 has reached RM3.6 billion," MOF said in a statement today.
The ministry said recipients could receive up to RM3,300 in total by August 2026 across STR Phases 1 to 3 and monthly Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) basic aid, excluding the one-off Sara payment for citizens aged 18 and above.
Starting this year, the aid framework was revamped to provide regular support, with STR paid quarterly and Sara delivered monthly to eligible individuals.
In the same statement, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government would ensure assistance reached those in need as the cost of living remained a challenge.
"With the cost of living still posing difficulties for some, the government will continue to ensure that aid reaches those who need it.
"That is why the number of households receiving STR has increased from 3.7 million at the start of the year to 3.9 million for Phase 3.
"STR and Sara help ease the daily needs of Malaysians while the government continues to implement reforms and strengthen the economy to raise incomes and living standards. Our goal is not just to provide aid, but to ensure that people's lives improve," he said.
The ministry said the restructuring of government finances and governance improvements enabled more state revenue to be channelled to those in need.
Total allocation for STR and Sara in 2026 amounts to RM15 billion, the highest in federal government history and nearly three times higher than the Bantuan Rakyat 1Malaysia (BR1M) payments in 2016.
Recipients with bank accounts will receive Phase 3 STR payments via direct credit starting today, while those without accounts can collect cash at any Bank Simpanan Nasional branch nationwide.
To minimise leakage, new applications and appeals for STR remain open throughout the year via the official portal at bantuantunai.hasil.gov.my, with FAQs available on the portal and Sara information at sara.gov.my.
The ministry advised the public to remain vigilant against fake links and scams, referring only to the official STR portal for accurate information.

Title: PKFZ rejects link between Chinese cargo and tariff evasion
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Port Klang Free Zone (PKFZ) said the presence of Chinese-linked businesses or international cargo within a Malaysian free zone should not, in itself, be interpreted as evidence of tariff evasion or illegal transshipment.
The statement came after a report by the United States Office of Trade and Manufacturing Policy (OTMP) identified Malaysia among more than 40 countries associated with
risks of illegal transshipment
.
In a report titled The Great Transshipment Scam: Rise, Scope, and Costs, the OTMP placed Malaysia in Tier 2 as a "scale leader with significant economic integration with China".
PKFZ chairman Lim Lip Eng said the free zone operated within a highly regulated customs and trade compliance framework as an integrated logistics hub.
"While Malaysia has been identified in the report as a country with significant trade and manufacturing links to China, it is important to clarify that Port Klang Free Zone (PKFZ) does not facilitate, endorse or condone any form of tariff evasion, false declaration, misrepresentation of origin or circumvention of international trade measures," he said.
He said all investors, manufacturers, traders and logistics operators seeking to establish operations within PKFZ were subject to stringent screening, due diligence and regulatory requirements.
"Their operations must comply with applicable Malaysian laws, customs requirements, free-zone regulations and the requirements imposed by the relevant government authorities," he said in a statement today.
Lim said matters relating to the origin of goods and export certification were governed by the appropriate national authorities and were not determined by PKFZ.
He said the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) had been the sole issuer of Non-Preferential Certificates of Origin (NPCO) for exports to the United States since May 6, 2025, with chambers of commerce and business associations no longer authorised to issue such certificates for US-bound exports.
[[nid:1511662]]
Lim said the certification process was comprehensive, requiring cost analysis, statutory declarations, company and manufacturing information, raw-material documentation, production flowcharts and supporting commercial documents, with approvals issued on a shipment basis for the relevant US-bound NPCOs.
"MITI has also enhanced its audit and verification mechanisms and works together with the Royal Malaysian Customs Department to address potential transshipment offences," he said.
"Therefore, the presence of Chinese-linked businesses or international cargo within a Malaysian free zone should not, in itself, be interpreted as evidence of tariff evasion or illegal transshipment," Lim said.
"Malaysia is a major regional manufacturing and logistics hub, and legitimate international trade naturally involves global supply chains, intermediate processing, consolidation and re-export activities," he said.
Lim said PKFZ remained committed to ensuring that its facilities were occupied by legitimate, compliant and commercially sustainable businesses.
He said PKFZ would fully cooperate with MITI, the Royal Malaysian Customs Department and other relevant authorities where there were regulatory concerns or indications of non-compliance, while taking appropriate action within its mandate.
"PKFZ also welcomes greater scrutiny and stronger enforcement against genuine cases of trade fraud," Lim said
He said a transparent, rules-based and properly regulated trading environment would ultimately protect legitimate investors and strengthen Malaysia's position as a trusted regional logistics and manufacturing hub.
He said Malaysia's regulatory framework, together with enhanced oversight by MITI and Customs, provided the necessary safeguards to distinguish legitimate value-added manufacturing and logistics activities from unlawful transshipment or tariff circumvention.

Title: Subang Airport flights suspended after helicopter catches fire during test
Article:
SUBANG: All flights to and from Subang Airport here have been suspended after a Kamov Ka-32S helicopter caught fire during an engine ground run today.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said the helicopter, registered as UR-CIT,
caught fire at 12.28pm
while undergoing an engine test as part of maintenance activities.
"The runway has since been closed, with all flights to and from the airport put on hold until further notice.
"Passengers are advised to contact their respective airlines," CAAM said in a statement.
The incident will be investigated by the Air Accident Investigation Bureau under the Transport Ministry in accordance with Part XXVI of the Civil Aviation Regulations 2016.
Earlier, the Selangor Fire and Rescue Department said four people escaped unhurt after the helicopter caught fire while preparing for take-off for the engine test following repairs.
Firemen from the airport fire and rescue service and the Bukit Jelutong Fire and Rescue Station were deployed to the scene.

Title: King told govt not to stop at TH, turn attention to Felda, says Anwar
Article:
AYER KEROH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today said the government will uncover alleged governance failures within the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda), which has been burdened by substantial debt.
Anwar, who is also PKR president, said the move was not aimed at punishing anyone prematurely, but at establishing the facts and ensuring that any wrongdoing was properly investigated.
He said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, had also instructed that investigations into governance failures should not end with Lembaga Tabung Haji.
"The King told me last week, 'Don't stop with Tabung Haji, continue the investigations.'
"His Majesty asked who is looking after Felda now, and I said I am. So, once Tabung Haji is dealt with, uncover what happened in Felda.
"Do not punish anyone before we have certainty. One of our problems is that we are quick to point fingers. Don't. Let the enforcement agencies investigate professionally and act professionally," he said in his policy speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here.
He said the government was currently shouldering nearly RM1 billion a year in Felda debt commitments, which he attributed to weaknesses in its previous management.
Anwar said his administration had to meet those financial commitments to ensure Felda's continued operations and safeguard the welfare of settlers.
He also called on enforcement agencies to act firmly and without fear or favour, regardless of the position, political affiliation, or background of those under investigation.
"There are those among the so-called intellectual elite who say the prime minister is now desperate and appears to be acting out of vengeance.
"So, according to them, if we take action, it is revenge. If we do not take action, it is a compromise and weakness.
"You can say whatever you want. My answer here, at the PKR Congress in Melaka, is that more decisive action begins now," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Penang PH-BN cooperation based on consensus, including DAP, says Chow
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: The decision to maintain cooperation between Pakatan Harapan and Barisan Nasional in Penang was made through a consensus among all component parties, including DAP, says Penang PH chairman Chow Kon Yeow.
He said there was no issue regarding the decision as it reflected the stance of the respective parties and was endorsed by the Penang PH Leadership Council.
"This decision was made by the PH Leadership Council, which I chaired, where, after their respective party meetings, the state chairs of Amanah, PKR, and DAP presented their positions to retain the PH-BN cooperation in Penang... which involves only one executive councillor.
"After hearing the views of each party, the PH Leadership Council reached a decision based on the consensus of all parties within PH... I believe every chair who attended represented their respective party. So there is no issue regarding that decision," he said after the Penang Chief Minister Tour programme at the Seberang Jaya Public Market here today.
He was commenting on a statement by DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng, who suggested he convene another internal meeting of Penang DAP delegates to gauge their stance on the state PH leadership's unconditional support for Umno's role in the state government.
When asked whether Penang DAP had held an internal meeting on continuing the PH-BN cooperation, Chow said he was not a member of the Penang DAP committee.
However, he said Penang DAP chairman Steven Sim had presented the party's stance on the matter during the state PH meeting.
"Steven reported the same stance as state Amanah chairman Muhammad Faiz Fadzil and PKR State Leadership Council chairman Datuk Dr Mohamad Abdul Hamid. They voiced the same united stance, so the state PH decided to maintain the cooperation," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: New Act to replace AUKU, says Zambry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A new, more comprehensive Act will be introduced to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU), said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abdul Kadir.
He said efforts to reform the higher education legal framework had been outlined in the Malaysia Higher Education Plan 2026–2035, launched in January, through the One Higher Education Act agenda.
Zambry said the abolition of AUKU must be followed by a new legal framework that is more comprehensive, progressive and suited to the needs of higher education today and in the future.
"I take note of the announcement by the prime minister regarding his statement on the abolition of AUKU during his presidential policy speech at the PKR's 2026 National Congress.
"AUKU is not merely an Act governing student affairs or freedom.
"It is the parent legislation that provides the basis for the establishment, administration and governance of universities and university colleges," Zambry said in a statement today.
He said the process would be carried out inclusively and comprehensively, taking into account the views of all stakeholders.
Zambry said these included university leaders, academics, public and private higher education institutions, industry players, polytechnics and community colleges, TVET providers, legal experts, students and other relevant parties.
"Our aim is not merely to abolish an Act, but to establish a more comprehensive and forward-looking higher education legal framework that strengthens institutional autonomy, academic freedom and the student voice, while ensuring that governance, accountability and excellence in higher education institutions continue to be upheld," he said.
Earlier today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had said the government would
abolish the Act
as part of its broader reform agenda, particularly in response to concerns raised by university students.
He said several amendments had already been made to give students greater freedom, but acknowledged that some remained dissatisfied and had submitted a memorandum calling for further changes.

Title: Pas says GE16 could be held anytime amid PH-BN tensions, Melaka polls
Article:
TUMPAT: Pas believes several factors could result in the 16th General Election (GE16) being held at any time, including the expiry of the Melaka state assembly's term and ties between Pakatan Harapan and Barisan Nasional.
Pas vice-president Datuk Idris Ahmad said the situation should serve as a wake-up call to all parties to be prepared for the possibility of an early election.
"One possible scenario is the Melaka state election, whose current term expires on Dec 27 this year.
"Another scenario is that the election could be held this year, before the first sitting of the new Parliament or the Sarawak state legislative assembly, which is due to begin on Feb 14, 2027," he said when met by reporters here last night.
The Bagan Serai member of parliament said the relationship between PH and BN was another factor that could influence the timing of the poll.
Describing the relationship as lukewarm, Idris said recent political developments indicated that cooperation between the two coalitions could face challenges.
He cited recent remarks by former Umno leader Khairy Jamaluddin, who claimed that ties between Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi were becoming increasingly strained.
"Khairy said Anwar and Zahid are increasingly at odds and that trust between them is at its lowest level.
"If the election is held today, it may already be difficult for PH. If it is delayed further, it could become even more difficult," he said.
Idris also pointed to the results of the Johor and Negri Sembilan state elections as contributing factors.
"In Johor, BN won 48 of the 56 seats, while PH won only eight. Recently, in Negri Sembilan, PH won only 11 of the 36 seats, while BN and its allies won 25.
"These are factors that we regard as pushing towards an election being held sooner," he said.
On reports that Perlis Umno was prepared to contest the next election on its own, Idris said decisions on political cooperation rested with the party's central leadership.
"It is not the states that will make the decision. The decision will be made at the central level.
"We have not discussed this with other states. We have not touched on it and have not discussed it yet.
"We have many other matters that are more important to deal with first. It is not a priority for us to discuss this at the moment," he said.
On Pas' preparations in Tumpat, Idris said the party's strength lay in its membership and grassroots organisation.
He said Pas had 155 branches in Tumpat with more than 13,000 members.
"Our strength is in our membership and branches. Tumpat has considerable strength, with 155 branches and more than 13,000 members. This strength must be maintained," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: AUKU abolition victory for student movement, says PKR Youth chief
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government's decision to abolish the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) has been described as a significant step towards restoring freedom and democratic space for university students.
Welcoming the announcement by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim said it was an important victory in the decades-long student movement for a freer and more democratic campus environment.
"Since the rise of the student movement in the late 1960s and early 1970s, including efforts to highlight poverty, social injustice and the plight of the underprivileged, students have proven that they are not merely occupants of lecture halls.
"They are part of the conscience of society," he said in a statement today.
Kamil said, however, the movement had also witnessed increasing restrictions on students through AUKU and other limitations on their activities and participation in public discourse.
He said successive generations of student activists had continued to call for greater freedom, more democratic campuses and the restoration of universities as spaces for intellectual discourse and academic courage.
"So, the Madani government's decision to move towards abolishing AUKU should be viewed in the context of this long history of struggle.
"It recognises that students should not be shaped by a culture of fear and excessive control.
"Students must be trusted to think, debate, hold differing views, criticise and offer solutions for the country," he said.
Kamil said university freedom did not mean freedom without responsibility but rather that a truly mature university should be capable of managing differences through knowledge, reasoned arguments and dialogue.
He said PKR Youth believed the abolition of AUKU should pave the way for more comprehensive higher education reforms and strengthening university autonomy.
He also urged Malaysian students and youths to view the development as proof that reform required political courage, patience and sustained support to translate it into meaningful change.
Earlier, Anwar had said the government would abolish the Act as part of its broader reform agenda, particularly in response to concerns raised by university students.
