Title: Urgent government changes to be announced starting late August, says Anwar
Article:
AYER KEROH: Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim will make several announcements regarding urgent changes to be implemented by the government starting late this month, culminating in the tabling of 2027 Budget in early October.
The prime minister, who is also Pakatan Harapan chairman, said the announcements would cover government policies, internal PH matters, cooperation within the unity government, and national programmes.
"So I hope tomorrow, after we listen to the debate today and tomorrow, I will address what I can regarding policy, internal party and PH matters, the unity government, and national programmes.
"Secondly, ahead of Independence Day on Aug 30, I will share my views before the historic day of Aug 31, and leading up to Malaysia Day on Sept 16 in Kuching, Sarawak. Following that, I will attempt to summarise several urgent changes that need to be implemented in the 2027 Budget this October.
"I have these three milestones, and God willing, we will execute them to the best of our ability," he said in his policy speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) today.
Also present were PKR and unity government leaders, including PKR deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar, Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) chairman Datuk Seri Hajiji Nor, and Amanah president Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu.
Meanwhile, Anwar, who is also the finance minister, acknowledged that the failure to translate policies effectively was not due to weak policies, but rather shortcomings in leadership communication.
"It is not the fault of the foundation; it is our own fault for lacking the skill to communicate effectively, and perhaps because certain matters have yet to be finalised.
"We cannot deny one thing: economic performance is good and all numbers are impressive, including Bank Negara's projection reaching up to six per cent for this quarter. But it will fail to touch and win the hearts of the people if our communication is weak," he said.
In addition, he said the government under his leadership had never sidelined Sabah and Sarawak, nor opposition-held states, in the national development agenda.
"To our friends in Sabah and Sarawak, I want to say that whatever our weaknesses may be, this is the first party and government in history that does not view the demands of Sabah and Sarawak as side issues.
"It is a national agenda, and we want to succeed as one nation. Sabah and Sarawak must be part of this nation-building programme," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar may make more announcements as early as tomorrow, says Fahmi
Article:
AYER KEROH: PKR information chief Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim may make several more announcements as early as tomorrow.
He said this as the party leadership considers proposals raised by delegates at the 2026 PKR National Congress, following Anwar's statement that the government would abolish the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU).
Among the proposals was a call for the monthly RON95 quota under the Budi95 targeted subsidy scheme to be restored to 300 litres, with some delegates proposing that it be increased further to 500 litres.
"Under Budi95, eligible Malaysians enjoy RON95 at RM1.99 per litre, with the initial monthly entitlement set at up to 300 litres.
"However, global economic and geopolitical conditions forced the government to review the figure and reduce it to 200 litres," Fahmi said when tabling the economy motion at the congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre here today.
Fahmi said the party leadership would take into account the views and proposals raised by delegates and consider how they could be translated into action.
"I'm not sure whether the delegates who asked for it to be increased back to 300 litres are here. Some have even asked for 500 litres. We will take all these views into consideration.
"As the PM, who is also our party's president, said earlier, the leadership must listen and translate what it hears into action.
"I believe that if the PM has mentioned this, it is not impossible that, before too long, perhaps as early as tomorrow, he may announce several other matters," he said.
Earlier, Anwar, who is also PKR president, announced in his policy speech that the government would
abolish AUKU
to provide university students with greater freedom. He said the matter would also be raised with the Cabinet on Wednesday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Motac cracks down on unlicensed tourism operators in KL, issues 15 notices
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — The Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (Motac) issued 15 inspection notices for various offences under the Tourism Industry Act 1992 (Act 482) during a two-day enforcement operation that began on Wednesday around Kuala Lumpur.
In a statement today, Motac said nine of the notices were issued under Subsection 5(2) for operating a tourism business without a valid licence.
“Three tourist locations, nine business premises and three individuals were inspected over the course of the operation.
“Intelligence work in collaboration with the Kuala Lumpur Tourist Guide Association (KLTGA) was also carried out to detect individuals suspected of carrying out tourist guide activities without valid licences. Enforcement action under Subsection 21(1) was taken against those found doing so,” the statement read.
The ministry said the operation also flagged other violations, including using private or unlicensed vehicles to ferry tourists, breaching licence conditions and doing business with unlicensed operators.
Private or unlicensed vehicles used for tourist transport that have been identified will be dealt with by the Land Public Transport Agency and Road Transport Department.
“Further investigations will be conducted before legal action is taken against individuals, entities, owners and other relevant parties involved,” the statement read.
Motac warned unlicensed parties not to offer tourism services, adding that offences under Act 482 are liable for compounds of up to RM250,000 or a fine of up to RM500,000, imprisonment of up to 10 years, or both, upon conviction.
“Motac remains committed to enforcing the law thoroughly, firmly and effectively, guided by the principles of good governance, fairness, integrity, and accountability, in line with the Malaysia Madani vision.
“The public and industry players are encouraged to channel any information on tourism activities suspected of violating laws and regulations through the Public Complaints Management System (SISPAA) at the following link: [https://motac.spab.gov.my/eApps/system/index.do,”](https://motac.spab.gov.my/eApps/system/index.do,”) the statement read. — Bernama

Title: Federal govt aims to cut Terengganu poor households to 20,000 by year-end
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 15 — The federal government aims to reduce the number of poor households in Terengganu to 20,000 by this December.
Deputy director-general of the Strategic Development, Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU), under the Prime Minister’s Department (ICU JPM), Datuk Norashiken Ishak, said as of August 13, the number of poor households in Terengganu was recorded at 24,100 households, compared to 26,800 households in early July.
“This effort is the result of coordinated actions by the Terengganu ICU JPM together with related agencies that can increase income, expand economic opportunities, and stabilise the lives of eKasih participants,” she said.
She said this to reporters after completing the Program Jelajah Kesejahteraan Rakyat 2026 for the Kuala Terengganu and Kuala Nerus zones, organised by the Terengganu ICU JPM, at the Hiliran People’s Housing Project (PPR) here today.
Norashiken said that additionally, her team has also succeeded in improving the living standards and welfare of the B40, especially eKasih participants, through 310 Rumah Kasih Ihsan projects implemented as of August this year, covering a total allocation of RM18.44 million.
She also said the total includes 161 new construction projects, 146 house renovation projects, and three new stilt house construction projects.
“So, InsyaAllah, we will continue this effort and contribution, and it is also the commitment of the Madani Government to ensure the well-being of the people,” she added.
Meanwhile, the Program Jelajah Kesejahteraan Rakyat 2026 for the Kuala Terengganu and Kuala Nerus zones, held today, brings together the services and interventions from various agencies to facilitate the community, especially the eKasih households, in obtaining assistance and services according to their needs.
Based on the value of Ihsan, the programmr was enlivened by the presence of 4,000 visitors, including 700 eKasih participants, and featured 18 government service booths for advisory services, eligibility checks and assistance matching. — Bernama

Title: Five PKR figures honoured with posthumous awards
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 15 — The contributions and sacrifices of five PKR figures were honoured posthumously at the 2026 PKR National Congress here today.
Four received the Bill Kayong Award, while the fifth was awarded the Dr Syed Husin Ali Pejuang Rakyat Award, introduced for the first time in recognition of the late Syed Husin’s contributions as a PKR founder and advocate of social justice.
The Bill Kayong Award was presented to the late Sapiah Zaini, former Miri Women’s chief; the late Hasbul Syafiqi Hasbullah, Keadilan Penang working secretary; and party activists, the late Syafiq Ali Abdullah@Abang Mani, and the late Muhammad Shahhanaz Nazarudin.
The award, named after the late Sarawak activist Bill Kayong, recognises individuals who have made significant contributions to the party’s struggle and grassroots work.
Syafiq’s older brother, Ahmad Sulaiman Selvarajah Abdullah, said the recognition meant a great deal to his family and strengthened their resolve to continue supporting PKR.
“…we are extremely happy and deeply honoured by this recognition of his immense contribution to Keadilan and the reform movement from the party’s founding in 1998 until today,” he said after accepting the award.
Hasbul Syafiqi’s mother, Normala Ghazali, said her son, better known as Black, had helped many friends in Penang and was known by party members across the country for always being willing to lend a hand.
“This recognition shows that many people still remember and cherish him to this day. To me, Black left this world having made a meaningful contribution to others,” she said.
Former senator Datuk Mustafa Kamal Mohd Yusoff, better known as Pak Mus, received the Dr Syed Husin Ali Pejuang Rakyat Award in recognition of his dedication and contribution to strengthening the party’s electoral machinery and understanding of election operations.
Meanwhile, the Tawau branch in Sabah took first place in the Highest Membership Registration Award, with the Bukit Gantang branch in Perak finishing second and the Indera Mahkota branch in Pahang third.
The number of new Keadilan ranting (sub-branches) rose to 1,354 this year, up from 520 last year, indicating increased grassroots participation among party members.
In the State and National Highest Number of Ranting Competition, Putatan branch in Sabah took first place, followed by Tanah Merah branch in Kelantan in second and Bangi branch in Selangor in third. — Bernama

Title: MOH to reopen four training institutes next year amid critical nurse shortage
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 15 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is strengthening three key strategies under the country’s health workforce reform to address the critical shortage of nurses, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad.
He said the three strategies involved increasing the number of nursing graduates, expanding career pathways and implementing direct recruitment and greater autonomy in staffing management.
“Of the 73,281 Grade U5 nurse positions, there are currently 10,557 vacancies in health facilities,” he said in his speech at the 2026 Ministry of Health Training Institute (ILKKM) Sabah Zone Convocation at the Chancellor’s Hall, Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS), today.
Dzulkefly said the move was important in meeting the country’s health workforce needs amid the increasingly complex challenges facing the health system.
Under the strategy to increase the nursing workforce, he said the intake of nurse trainees had been increased to 3,000 a year from 2025.
“To expand this strategy, the MOH aims to outsource up to 2,000 trainees a year to Public Higher Education Institutions (IPTA) and Private Higher Education Institutions (IPTS),” he said.
In addition, he said four ILKKM branches in Kuantan, Kuala Terengganu, Muar and Penang would reopen by October 2027, providing additional capacity for about 500 trainees.
“This brings the total capacity of the Diploma in Nursing programme to 5,500 trainees a year,” he added.
For the second strategy, Dzulkefly said the MOH would roll out 15 On-the-Job Training (OJT) programmes this September to enable staff to enhance their expertise without having to leave their workplace for long periods.
“The ministry is also expanding the career pathway for community nurses to become nurses through the Transition Diploma,” he said.
Under the third strategy, Dzulkefly said the Public Service Department (JPA) had approved an exemption from Interim Contract Appointments for eligible ILKKM Diploma in Nursing graduates.
“This means that all ILKKM Diploma in Nursing graduates who have successfully completed the programme and are registered with the Nursing Board of Malaysia will be absorbed directly to permanent positions,” he said.
Dzulkefly said that, since July 9, 2026, the ministry had also been granted autonomy in staffing management to reduce bureaucracy and facilitate the direct placement of graduates in the field. — Bernama

Title: Sabah hospital sexual harassment case: MOH moves director out, complainant under treatment, PSD to decide next step
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 15 — The Health Ministry has completed its internal investigation into an alleged sexual harassment case involving a Sabah hospital director and transferred the officer to a medical post at the Sabah Health Department.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry had also submitted its report to the Public Service Department (PSD), which has jurisdiction over further action based on the officer’s grade,
The New Straits Times
reported.
“Administratively, the ministry has completed the internal investigation. Among the actions taken was the transfer of the director to a medical officer’s position in the medical division of the Sabah Health Department,” he was quoted as saying at a press conference after the ministry’s Training Institutes convocation at Universiti Malaysia Sabah here today.
Dzulkefly said the alleged victim had been given full support and psychiatric treatment and had since returned to a better working environment.
“The official report from the department has been submitted to Public Service Department, based on the officer’s grade, as it has its own jurisdiction and authority to handle this matter,” he said.
The case was raised publicly last month by Kapayan assemblyman Chin Teck Ming and Sabah Warisan Health Bureau chief Dr Istefan Koh over alleged wrongdoing involving the hospital director.
Sabah police commissioner Datuk Jauteh Dikun had also confirmed that a police report was lodged earlier this year.
Dzulkefly said the ministry had taken administrative action after completing its internal probe, while any further disciplinary action would fall within the PSD’s jurisdiction.

Title: Sabah-based KDM cuts ties with GRS govt, says it’s time to win back grassroots
Article:
KINARUT, Aug 15 — Parti Kesejahteraan Demokratik Masyarakat (KDM) today pulled its support for the Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS)-led state government, signalling a shift in the party’s political direction ahead of the next general election.
KDM acting president Priscella Peter said the decision was made by the party’s supreme council during its annual meeting today, local media reported.
“What is important is that, in preparation for the next general election, KDM, together with its supreme council, has decided to move forward without being part of the GRS government,” she was quoted by news outlet Free Malaysia Today as saying at press conference in Papar.
She said the decision, which was not made lightly, was intended to make KDM’s position clear to the public and its grassroots supporters.
Priscella said the party had been affected by what happened after the previous state election, prompting it to make its position known well before the next polls.
“What happened after the last state election has certainly had an impact on our grassroots,” she said.
She said KDM wanted to show that its political decisions were not driven solely by the timing of elections, but reflected a longer-term commitment to its supporters.
“We need to take action beforehand to demonstrate our commitment and regain the trust of our grassroots,” she said.
The move comes a week after Warisan president Datuk Seri Shafie Apdal said his party was in discussions with KDM and Parti Solidariti Tanah Airku over a possible cooperation for the 16th general election.
Shafie said no agreement had been reached, but any pact involving Warisan would safeguard Sabah’s rights and interests.
KDM contested the November 2025 state election independently and won one seat, Paginatan, before subsequently aligning itself with the GRS administration led by Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor.

Title: Onn Hafiz: Bangsa Johor rental deposit aid of RM1,000 to roll out next year
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 15 — The Johor government is expected to introduce the RM1,000 Bangsa Johor rental deposit assistance next year to help people in the state who face difficulties coming up with the upfront payment for accommodation.
Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the initiative, implemented through the Johor State Housing Development Corporation (PKPJ), is being introduced in response to complaints from tenants who face difficulties paying the upfront amount or rental deposit.
He said applications for the initiative would also be open to federal civil servants serving in Johor, such as teachers, nurses, medical officers, police personnel and members of the armed forces.
“Apart from rental assistance, there have been calls for the government to consider rental deposit assistance, especially for those who have just started working... perhaps many of them cannot afford it yet.
“We want to expand this assistance so that it benefits not only Bangsa Johor but also those who have recently moved to Johor, particularly federal civil servants. They serve in Johor, are part of Bangsa Johor and are working for us,” he said.
He said this at a press conference after the Phase 5 of the Perumahan Kasih Johor Initiative ceremony at the Larkin Indoor Arena Stadium here today.
Onn Hafiz said the first phase of the rental deposit assistance would target about 10,000 recipients.
Eligible recipients would also be entitled to Rental Assistance of RM2,500, bringing the total assistance available to RM3,500 per person. Eligibility covers individuals residing and working in the state.
He said further details, as well as new housing products, would be announced during the tabling of the Johor Budget in November.
At today’s ceremony, RM22 million was allocated for Phase 5, covering 6,000 recipients of various housing assistance schemes, while Phase 6, scheduled for next month, is expected to benefit another 5,000 recipients.
Overall, the Johor government has spent RM337 million on its housing agenda since 2022, benefiting nearly 100,000 recipients statewide. — Bernama

Title: DoE detects seven hotspots in East Malaysia as transboundary haze worsens air quality
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — A total of seven hotspots were detected in the country, with five in Sarawak and two in Sabah, as air quality deteriorates in several areas of Sarawak, which are currently recording Air Pollutant Index (API) readings at unhealthy levels.
Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said that, based on the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) report dated August 14, a total of 226 hotspots were also detected in Kalimantan, while another five were recorded in Sumatra.
As of 11am today, nine areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy API readings, with Kuching recording the highest at 164, followed by Samarahan (161), Serian IPD (160), Bintulu and Sarikei (157), Sri Aman (153), Sibu (152), Mukah (151) and Samalaju (118).
“The deterioration in air quality was caused by the movement of haze from various directions, including moderate to dense transboundary smoke plumes from clusters of hotspots in West Kalimantan moving northwards into the western part of the state.
“Moderate to dense localised smoke plumes were also observed, originating from hotspots in large parts of Kalimantan, central Sarawak and central Sumatra,” she said in a statement today.
She said several air quality monitoring stations in West Kalimantan as well as western and central Sarawak also recorded unhealthy readings.
However, ASMC said the full extent of the hotspot and haze situation in the region could not be determined due to cloud cover.
In view of the situation, Azuri Azizah said the DOE had stepped up enforcement action and daily patrols in areas prone to open burning, in addition to monitoring API readings from time to time.
“The National Open Burning Action Plan and National Haze Action Plan have also been activated to coordinate the actions of government agencies in addressing open burning and haze situations,” she said.
She advised landowners to monitor areas that are prone to and frequently affected by fires, including landfill sites, forests, peatlands, plantations, agricultural and industrial areas, and to take measures to prevent intrusion by irresponsible parties.
The public was also reminded not to carry out open burning and to report any cases of open burning or fires to the Fire and Rescue Department at 999 or the DOE’s toll-free line at 1-800-88-2727. — Bernama

Title: If you’re naughty, we will know it, mayor warns as Kota Kinabalu adds 1,600 CCTV cameras to catch vandals
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Aug 15 — A total of 1,600 closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras will be installed across the city soon as City Hall (DBKK) moves to strengthen surveillance and protect public assets from vandalism.
Mayor Datuk Seri Dr Sabin Samitah said funding for the project had been secured, with installation expected to begin soon.
“The expanded surveillance would also help safeguard public assets such as the newly unveiled ‘Remembering Australia Place’ mural from vandalism,” he said during the launch of the mural, Friday.
The project commemorates the historical links between Australia and Sabah, including the contribution of Australian personnel to the rebuilding of Jesselton after the Second World War, while Sabin hoped the artwork would become a vibrant and meaningful heritage destination for Kota Kinabalu.
The “Remembering Australia Place” mural, located on the Wisma Intiutama building in central Kota Kinabalu, was produced by local community arts organisation Pillars of Sabah, with support from the Australian High Commission and involvement from teachers and students of SMK Sanzac.
The mural is intended to tell the story of Australia-Sabah friendship, remembrance and people-to-people ties, with a QR code also planned on site to provide visitors with additional information about the area’s historical significance.
Sabin also said the Kota Kinabalu International Mayors’ Dialogue 2026 would bring together mayors, city leaders, policymakers, development partners and other stakeholders to exchange ideas and practical experiences on the challenges and opportunities facing cities.
He said the dialogue, scheduled for October, reflected Kota Kinabalu’s aspiration to strengthen city-to-city diplomacy and international cooperation, particularly in sustainable and resilient cities, smart city development, climate action, tourism, urban liveability and inclusive economic growth.
In this regard, Sabin invited Australian High Commission representatives and Australian city leaders to support and participate in the international dialogue, noting that two mayors from the United States had confirmed their participation.
He said Australian participation would provide an opportunity to strengthen practical cooperation and relationships between Kota Kinabalu and Australian cities, and expressed hope that the Australian High Commission could help facilitate the attendance of Australian city leaders.
Kota Kinabalu MP and Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Datuk Chan Foong Hin hoped the mural would help stimulate the arrival of more Australian tourists to Sabah, particularly by strengthening awareness of the historical and contemporary connections between the two sides.
He also welcomed calls to restore direct flights between Australia and Sabah, saying he would raise the matter with his party secretary-general, who is also the Transport Minister. — Daily Express

Title: Threat ends as Sabah wildlife officers kill 14-foot croc near in Sipitang river near jetty to Labuan
Article:
SIPITANG, August 15 — A 14-foot male crocodile was caught and shot dead by the Sabah Wildlife Department (JHL) on Thursday, bringing relief to residents who had been living in fear of the reptile at Kampung Tanjung Pagar.
A village resident said they were grateful for the department’s swift action in dealing with the crocodile, which had earlier been caught using a fishing line.
The crocodile was frequently spotted at the mouth of the river near Kg Tanjung Pagar before it was shot dead and handed over to a licensed crocodile hunter.
However, residents have been warned to remain cautious as other crocodiles could still be in the area.
“There could still be other crocodiles there, so residents need to be careful when they are near the river, as crocodiles can attack suddenly and prey on those who are unaware,” the resident said.
The area is also near the boat jetty serving passengers travelling to Labuan, who have been urged to exercise caution when boarding passenger boats.
The residents thanked the Wildlife Department for successfully capturing and eliminating the crocodile and hoped operations would continue to deal with other crocodiles that could pose a threat to residents and boat passengers.
Meanwhile, villagers at Kg Pelakat Skim, together with the Wildlife Department, have been setting fishing lines in a drain after crocodiles were spotted there.
According to residents, a crocodile had frequently been seen swimming in the drain, raising concerns over the potential danger, particularly to children who often spend time near the area, including those who enjoy fishing.
“We advise residents to be more careful when approaching or playing near the drain,” they said.
The residents said they had lodged a complaint with the Wildlife Department regarding the crocodile, prompting officers to visit the area and set fishing lines in an effort to catch it. — Daily Express

Title: Finance Ministry to roll out RM1.2b in STR cash aid for 5.3 million recipients from today
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 15 — The Ministry of Finance (MOF) said Phase 3 payments of the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) cash aid will be disbursed in stages starting today to 5.3 million recipients, with an allocation of RM1.2 billion.
The number of recipients has grown by 300,000 since the start of the year, when it stood at five million. Of these, 3.9 million are low- and middle-income households, and 1.4 million are single senior citizens.
“The Phase 3 payments range from RM150 to RM600, depending on income and number of children, while single senior citizens will receive RM150.
“Overall, the total disbursement for the first three phases of 2026 has reached RM3.6 billion,” MOF said in a statement today.
The ministry said, depending on the category they fall under, recipients can collect up to RM3,300 in total by August 2026, combining STR Phases 1 to 3 and the monthly SARA basic aid. This amount does not include the one-off SARA payment for all Malaysian citizens aged 18 and above.
Starting this year, the assistance has been revamped to provide more regular support. STR is paid out quarterly, while SARA delivers monthly basic aid to those who qualify.
In the same statement, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government will continue to ensure that assistance reaches those in need, as the cost of living remains a challenge.
“With the cost of living still posing difficulties for some, the government will continue to ensure that aid reaches those who need it.
“That is why the number of households receiving STR has increased from 3.7 million at the start of the year to 3.9 million for Phase 3.
“STR and SARA help ease the daily needs of Malaysians, while the government continues to implement reforms and strengthen the economy to raise incomes and living standards. Our goal is not just to provide aid, but to ensure that people’s lives improve,” he said.
Meanwhile, MOF said the restructuring of government finances and improvements in governance have enabled more state revenue to be channeled to those in need.
Total allocation for STR and SARA in 2026 amounts to RM15 billion, the highest in the Federal government’s history and nearly three times higher than the Bantuan Rakyat 1Malaysia (BR1M) payments in 2016.
Recipients with bank accounts will receive their Phase 3 STR payments via direct credit starting today. For those without bank accounts, payments can be collected in cash at any Bank Simpanan Nasional branch nationwide.
To minimise leakage, new applications and appeals for STR remain open throughout the year via the official STR portal at bantuantunai.hasil.gov.my.
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) on STR are also available on the portal, while SARA FAQs can be found at sara.gov.my.
MOF also advised the public to remain vigilant against fake links and scams, and to refer only to the official STR portal for the latest information. — Bernama

Title: He saw the crash online and knew something was wrong: Father loses wife, son in Temerloh crash
Article:
TEMERLOH, Aug 15 — A routine wait for his wife’s arrival turned into a frantic search for answers after Saifulnizam Sulaiman realised she had not responded to his messages or calls for hours.
Saifulnizam, 39, was in Seremban for work while his wife, Nur Fatima Syuhada Abdullah, 39, and their 12-year-old son, Muhammad Fattah Aisy Naufal Saifulnizam, were travelling from Jerantut to join him during the school holidays.
“I sent her a message at about 5pm, but there was no reply, and after finishing work at about 7pm, I saw that the message was still unread and my calls were also unanswered,” he told Berita Harian when met at the forensic unit of Sultan Haji Ahmad Shah Hospital here today.
He said his wife would normally keep him updated on their location and journey, and had never failed to answer his messages or calls during their 14 years of marriage.
“That’s why when the message was not read for several hours, I felt that something bad had happened,” he said.
His worst fears grew after he came across social media posts about a crash along Jalan Temerloh-Triang.
“It was then that I saw the accident on Jalan Temerloh-Triang on social media, and the first thing that came to my mind was, ‘That’s my wife and son,’” he said.
Saifulnizam said he contacted relatives in Temerloh to try to reach his wife, but they were also unable to get through to her.
He then drove from Seremban to Temerloh to find out what had happened.
Nur Fatima and Muhammad Fattah were killed after the car they were travelling in collided with a diesel tanker at about 4.30pm yesterday at Kilometre 9 of Jalan Temerloh-Triang.
Both vehicles caught fire following the collision.
Saifulnizam said his wife and son had left Jerantut at about 2pm and were heading to Seremban to help him with his business during the school holidays.
The tanker was carrying 32,000 litres of diesel and was believed to have skidded before colliding with the car.
Videos of the crash circulated on social media, showing both vehicles engulfed in flames shortly after the collision.

Title: New ‘One Higher Education Act’, launched in January, to replace UUCA, Zambry confirms
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 15 — A more comprehensive national higher education legislative framework to replace the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA) has been outlined under the Malaysia Higher Education Plan (RPTM) 2026-2035, said Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir.
He said the effort was part of the agenda for establishing the One Higher Education Act, which was launched in January 2026.
Zambry said the Higher Education Ministry was taking into account the need to reform the national higher education legislative framework by drafting a new, more comprehensive act to replace UUCA.
“I take note of the Prime Minister’s announcement on the repeal of UUCA during his presidential policy speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress,” he said in a statement today.
Zambry said UUCA was more than legislation governing student affairs and freedom, as it provided the basis for the establishment, administration and governance of universities and university colleges.
“Therefore, its repeal must be accompanied by a new legal framework that is more comprehensive, progressive and aligned with the current and future needs of higher education,” he said.
He said the process would be carried out in an inclusive and comprehensive manner, taking into account the views of all stakeholders, including university leaders, academics, public and private higher education institutions, industry players, polytechnics, community colleges, TVET providers, legal experts and students.
According to Zambry, the move was aimed not just at repealing UUCA, but at establishing a more comprehensive and forward-looking higher education legislative framework that would strengthen institutional autonomy, academic freedom and student voice, while preserving governance, accountability and excellence across higher education institutions.
He said the move was part of the higher education transformation under the RPTM 2026-2035 aimed at ensuring Malaysia’s higher education system remains relevant and dynamic amid changes in the global education landscape.
Earlier, Anwar said the government would repeal UUCA to provide greater freedom and democratic space for the student movement in the country.
He said the move followed a memorandum and views presented by student leaders calling for comprehensive changes to the Act. — Bernama

Title: Helicopter catches fire during engine test at Subang airport, four escape but one hit by debris
Article:
SUBANG JAYA, Aug 15 — A Kamov Ka-32 helicopter caught fire during an engine test at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport here today, with four people escaping and one person reportedly injured after being struck by debris outside the aircraft.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) confirmed the incident in an X post, saying the runway was closed following the incident and further updates would be issued.
“The fire occurred as the helicopter was about to take off for the purpose of engine testing after repairs,” Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said in a statement today.
He said firefighters found the helicopter, registered as UR-CIT in Ukraine, fully engulfed in flames when they arrived after receiving an emergency call at 12.30pm.
The four people on board managed to escape from the helicopter during the fire.
One other person, who was outside the aircraft, was reportedly injured after being struck by debris from the helicopter.
The airport’s Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting Service team also assisted in the firefighting operation.
Five firefighters from the Bukit Jelutong Fire and Rescue Station were deployed with a Fire Rescue Tender to the scene.
The circumstances surrounding the incident are still being investigated.

Title: MoH: No significant rise in haze-related illnesses yet
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 15 — Malaysia has not recorded a significant increase in haze-related illnesses so far, but the Ministry of Health (MOH) does not rule out a rise in cases if air quality worsens or the haze persists.
The MOH said no increase had been recorded so far in the three types of haze-related illnesses, namely upper respiratory tract infections (URTI), asthma and conjunctivitis, monitored through sentinel health facilities.
“Monitoring so far has found no significant increase in cases in any state compared with the situation before the haze,” the minisry told Bernama.
In Sarawak, the MOH said monitoring at 12 sentinel health clinics recorded a decline in URTI cases, from 1,473 in Epidemiological Week (EW) 31, before the haze, to 1,347 in EW 32.
Asthma cases fell from 195 to 122, while conjunctivitis cases rose from 15 to 43.
According to the MOH, children, the elderly and those with chronic illnesses are at greater risk of being affected by haze.
It said children have a higher respiratory rate, resulting in greater exposure to haze particles and potential health effects, while they are also less able to make appropriate decisions, particularly in dangerous situations.
Haze can have adverse effects on chronic conditions such as asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and heart disease.
The ministry further said that fine particles in haze can penetrate deep into the lungs, triggering inflammation and shortness of breath, while increasing the risk of heart attacks, acute attacks and hospitalisation.
“Therefore, people with chronic diseases should avoid exposure to haze to prevent their conditions from worsening. They should also follow their doctors’ advice and take their medication regularly,” it said.
The MOH anticipates an increase in haze-related illnesses if the haze persists or air quality worsens, with all health facilities instructed to remain on alert.
The ministry also said it is monitoring haze-related illnesses at health facilities located near the Department of Environment’s air quality monitoring stations.
A total of 68 health facilities have been selected to monitor haze-related illnesses, with data collection increased from weekly before the haze to daily during the haze.
The MOH said that so far, there had been no significant increase in hospital admissions or emergency cases linked to the haze.
However, the ministry said it would continue monitoring the situation and take appropriate action to treat patients with haze-related illnesses.
Meanwhile, the MOH advised the public to avoid outdoor physical activities to reduce exposure to haze, as increased breathing rates during physical activity can result in more suspended particles entering the respiratory tract.
“The public is also advised to stay indoors as much as possible and, if they need to go outside, limit their time outdoors and use appropriate face masks.
“Windows should also be kept closed to reduce haze entering homes or buildings,” it said, urging the public to avoid smoking and other activities that could increase indoor air pollution, and to keep their surroundings clean.
When driving, the public is also advised to use air conditioning in recirculation mode and drink plenty of plain water, with at least eight glasses a day recommended to stay hydrated.
The MOH said indoor air quality can also be improved by using air conditioning and high-efficiency air filters or purifiers to remove fine particles and prevent the entry of polluted air from outside.
“Those who are unwell are advised to seek immediate treatment at the nearest health facility, while information on measures to reduce the health effects of haze is available on the MOH’s InfoSihat website,” it said.
The MOH also urged the public not to engage in open burning or allow irresponsible parties to trespass on their land or premises for such activities. — Bernama

Title: MACC detains seven in Tabung Haji RCI probe, including senior executives and shipping company CEO
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has detained seven people as part of its investigation into the findings of the RCI report on Tabung Haji (TH).
According to sources, the suspects, comprising a chief executive officer, a former director, a director and four former TH senior executives, were arrested separately between 3pm and 10.30pm last night at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya.
“The first suspect, a shipping company CEO with a ‘Datuk’ title in his 60s, was arrested on suspicion of submitting documents with false details when making payments to TH. It involved falsifying a petroleum company contract to benefit his own firm.
“The second suspect is a construction company director with a ‘Datuk’ title, also in his 60s. He is suspected of deceiving TH officers into investing in a construction company with a promise that the firm had potential to be listed on Bursa Malaysia,” the source said.
The third suspect, a former company director with a ‘Datuk Seri’ title in his 60s, was arrested on suspicion of being involved in the same matter as the second suspect, the source added.
Meanwhile, four former senior TH management members, aged between 50 and 60, including one with a “Datuk Seri” title and a woman, were arrested on suspicion of being involved in corrupt practices leading TH into a hotel lease with a company in Saudi Arabia worth SR2.49 billion, resulting in losses to the pilgrimage fund.
Sources said only the shipping company CEO and construction company director were remanded, while the other five suspects were released on MACC bail for health reasons.
Magistrate Ahmad Afiq Hasan issued a five-day remand order until August 19 for both suspects after allowing MACC’s application at the Putrajaya Magistrates’ Court this morning.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrests when contacted, and said the case is being investigated under Sections 18 and 16(a)(A) of the MACC Act 2009. — Bernama

Title: Anwar signals key changes before Budget 2027, first announcements due Monday
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he would soon announce several urgent changes that the government plans to implement before the tabling of Budget 2027 in early October.
He said the changes would involve government policies, internal issues within Pakatan Harapan (PH) and cooperation among parties in the federal unity government.
Anwar, who is PKR president, said he would begin sharing details of some of the changes from the day after tomorrow, ahead of Merdeka Day and Malaysia Day celebrations.
“I will also announce the other changes in the upcoming 2027 Budget in October,” he said when delivering his Presidential Policy Speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here today.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the failure to effectively communicate government policies was not due to weaknesses in the policies themselves, but rather a breakdown in communication at the leadership level.
He said there was a need to communicate the policies more effectively, as some matters may have been overlooked.
“At the same time, we cannot deny that the country’s economic performance is good.
“The figures are very favourable, including Bank Negara's projection of reaching six per cent for this quarter.
“However, this achievement still cannot win the hearts of the people if our communication is weak,” he said.
Meanwhile, Anwar expressed his appreciation to Deputy Prime Minister and Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi for his determination to cooperate in forming the unity government.
He also expressed his appreciation to Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg and Sabah leaders for their willingness to support the formation of the federal government.
“Despite the differences of opinion between the parties in the unity government, all parties need to understand that changes need to be implemented in stages.
“We are not a government that governs alone and different states have different needs. So, we need to negotiate before any changes can be made,” he said, adding that certain parties pushing for immediate change had also failed to do so when they were in power.
He did not identify those he was referring to.
Anwar pointed out that the coalition government must determine its priorities in implementing its reform agenda without neglecting political stability, national security and the well-being of the people.

Title: ‘I take the peaceful path’: Anwar dismisses Khairy’s claim of rift with Zahid
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has stressed that his relationship with Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi remains good.
He said former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin’s claim that their relationship had deteriorated was merely the former Rembau Member of Parliament’s personal view.
“That is his personal view. He always looks at things from the perspective of conflict. I look at things from the perspective of peace... and that is the difference. He takes the confrontational path, while I take the peaceful path,” he told reporters after delivering his presidential address at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) here today.
Anwar, who is also PKR president and Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman, said he had also expressed his appreciation in his speech at the congress for the role played by Ahmad Zahid, as Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman and Umno president, in facilitating the formation of the Unity Government following the 15th General Election (GE15).
“That is why I thanked Datuk Seri Zahid and Umno in my speech earlier for their role, as BN chairman, in establishing the Unity Government at the initial stage,” he said.
Yesterday, Khairy claimed that trust between Anwar and Ahmad Zahid was now at its lowest level since the Unity Government was formed in 2022.
Khairy claimed that the situation followed increasingly challenging relations between BN and PH, particularly after BN chose to cooperate with Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the Negeri Sembilan State Election (PRN).
Elaborating, the Prime Minister said any differences of opinion within a party or between parties forming the Unity Government could be resolved through discussions and a peaceful approach. — Bernama

Title: Penang Pakatan’s decision to stay with BN had component parties’ consensus, says Chow Kon Yeow
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Aug 15 — Penang Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) decision to maintain its cooperation with Barisan Nasional (BN) was reached by consensus among all its component parties, including DAP, state PH chairman Chow Kon Yeow reportedly said today.
According to
Berita Harian
, Chow said the respective positions of DAP, PKR and Amanah had been presented before the state PH Leadership Council endorsed the continued partnership.
“This was a decision of the PH Leadership Council, which I chair, and after hearing the views of every party, the council reached a consensus in line with their respective positions,” he was quoted as saying after an event at the Seberang Jaya Public Market here.
He was responding to DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng’s proposal for another meeting of Penang DAP delegates to gauge their position on the state PH leadership’s support for Umno’s role in the state government.
Chow said he could not comment on whether DAP had held an internal meeting on the matter because he was not a member of its state committee, but added that Penang DAP chairman Steven Sim had conveyed the party’s position to PH.
He said Sim, Penang Amanah chairman Muhammad Faiz Fadzil and state PKR Leadership Council chairman Datuk Dr Mohamad Abdul Hamid had expressed the same position, leading PH to retain the cooperation.

Title: Anwar: UUCA repeal proposal goes to Cabinet next week
Article:
AYER KEROH, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today his proposal to repeal the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA) will be brought to the Cabinet next Wednesday for consideration.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the Cabinet would need to deliberate on his proposal first,
Berita Harian
reported when reporters asked if the repeal had already been approved.
“I will bring it to the Cabinet on Wednesday,” he replied after delivering his presidential policy speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre here.
Anwar had earlier announced during his speech that the government would repeal UUCA, citing continued objections from university students among the reasons for the move.
The announcement came after several amendments to the Act over the years, including changes in 2012 that allowed students to participate in activities organised by political parties outside campus.
UUCA has been amended seven times since it was introduced in 1971, including further amendments in 1975, 1983, 1996 and 2009.
The latest amendments in 2024 removed disciplinary authority over students at public universities from vice-chancellors, with such matters instead decided by Student Disciplinary Committees through changes to Section 16B.
The 2024 amendments also revised Section 15A to allow student representative councils and student bodies to raise funds and receive contributions, subject to prevailing written laws and regulations.

Title: PKR Youth backs UUCA repeal, urges students to speak up for wider reforms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — PKR Youth today backed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement to repeal the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA), but said the move should pave the way for wider reforms to strengthen university autonomy, academic freedom and student rights.
The party’s youth wing also urged students to continue speaking up and acting as a check and balance on the government, despite being part of Anwar’s own party.
“To Malaysian students, do not stop speaking up. Do not stop thinking. Do not stop being a check and balance on the country,” PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim said in a statement today.
Kamil said the repeal should open the way for stronger university autonomy, academic freedom, freedom of association and freedom of expression, as well as greater space for students to determine the direction of their own movements.
He said university freedom should not be interpreted as freedom without responsibility, but should allow campuses to manage differences through knowledge, argument and dialogue.
Kamil said universities should produce graduates who were willing to question established norms, challenge conventional thinking and defend what they believed was right responsibly.
PKR Youth described Anwar’s announcement as an important milestone in the decades-long struggle by Malaysian students for freer and more democratic campuses.
Kamil said the government’s decision recognised that students should not be shaped by a culture of fear and excessive control, but trusted to think, debate, disagree, criticise and offer solutions for the country.
He said students and young Malaysians should view the development as proof that reform required political courage, patience and sustained support to turn announcements into meaningful change.
Kamil also called on the Madani government to continue pursuing institutional reforms, saying students should remain among the key forces monitoring, pressing for and helping to implement those changes.
The call for students to remain a check and balance is notable as PKR Youth is part of Anwar’s own party, even as it backs his decision to repeal UUCA.
Kamil said reform did not end with a single announcement or the repeal of one law, with further changes still needed in higher education and other institutions.
He urged Malaysian students to continue voicing their views, thinking critically and holding the country’s institutions to account.
Anwar announced the repeal of UUCA at the 2026 PKR National Congress in Ayer Keroh today, saying previous amendments had given students greater freedom but had not addressed all their concerns.
UUCA, introduced in 1971, has been amended seven times, including changes in 2012 that allowed students to participate in political party activities outside campus.
The latest amendments in 2024 included changes to student disciplinary procedures, with such matters at public universities shifted from the vice-chancellor to Student Disciplinary Committees, as well as expanded powers for student representative councils and student bodies to collect funds and receive contributions subject to prevailing laws and regulations.

Title: Anwar announces special Madani F1 tickets for MyKad holders from RM200
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Malaysians holding MyKad will be able to attend all three days of Formula 1’s return to Sepang through special Tiket Madani priced from RM200, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced today.
He said the initiative would give more Malaysians the opportunity to experience Formula 1 in person when the race returns to Sepang in October.
“Alhamdulillah, following discussions and agreement with Bahrain, the government is pleased to announce special Madani Tickets for MyKad holders priced from as little as RM200 for access throughout the three-day event,” he said in a Facebook post today.
The Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit is scheduled for October 2 to 4, marking the sport’s return to Malaysia for the first time since 2017.
Tickets announced earlier this week included three-day passes for Malaysian citizens ranging from RM200 for the G Hillstand to RM2,083.40 for the Main Grandstand.
Anwar said the initiative was aimed at giving more Malaysians the chance to experience Formula 1 directly at Sepang.
“Hopefully, this initiative will give more Malaysians the opportunity to experience Formula 1 in person at Sepang,” he said.
Further details on the Madani Tickets will be announced by SIC soon, he added.

Title: Anwar says allocations for Sabah, Sarawak, Kedah and Kelantan increased under Madani govt
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today dismissed claims by certain quarters that the Madani Government is sidelining several states.
Instead, he stressed that allocations to each state differ according to priorities and have continued to increase under his administration.
“Sabah’s expenditure has increased by 35 per cent in the three years since we took over the government. Before that, in the preceding years, did the state government raise the issue? No... Allocations for Sabah, Sarawak, Kedah and Kelantan have increased overall.
“Terengganu’s allocation rose from RM6 billion in 2022 to RM8.1 billion this year, as did Perlis, Johor and others. Johor’s allocation increased from RM10.2 billion in 2022 to RM14.6 billion in 2026,” he said when delivering his Presidential Policy Speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre (MITC) in Ayer Keroh here today.
Anwar said the Federal allocation to Sabah had also increased by 35 per cent, from RM13 billion in 2022 to RM17.6 billion in 2026, while Sarawak’s allocation rose from RM10.2 billion in 2022 to RM15.1 billion, an increase of 48 per cent. — Bernama

Title: Missing three days, found 140km away, back with families but KL police still investigating case of two Alor Gajah MRSM students
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Two 16-year-old MRSM Alor Gajah students who went missing for three days have been reunited with their families.
Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the two teenagers were found at about 10.30pm yesterday at Central Market here — nearly 140km away from the Melaka school campus.
“The cause and circumstances surrounding the incident are still under police investigation,” he was quoted by Berita Harian as saying today.
The students, Siti Nur Aaira Aidi and Nur Aisy Humaira Mohd Saad, were reported missing after a teacher lodged a police report at 10.46pm on August 11.
Fadil said the two had previously sought treatment at a health clinic in Alor Gajah after feeling unwell.
“They were taken to Hospital Kuala Lumpur after being found for further medical examination before being handed back to their families,” he added.
MARA chairman Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki took to Facebook yesterday appealing for public assistance to pray for the safe return of the two students, later reporting that the girls had been found by police.

Title: Not all of Umno can be guilty: Pakatan Harapan should not use an overly generic approach – Phar Kim Beng
Article:
AUGUST 15 — One of the greatest dangers in Malaysian politics is the temptation to convert institutional wrongdoing into collective political guilt.
This is particularly important when Pakatan Harapan (PH) discusses Umno and the controversies associated with previous Barisan Nasional administrations.
The principle should be straightforward: not all of Umno can be guilty simply because some Umno leaders, office-holders or political appointees may have been implicated in wrongdoing.
If Malaysia is serious about becoming a mature constitutional democracy, responsibility must be compartmentalised. Investigations must identify particular decisions, particular offices, particular individuals and particular periods. Evidence must determine culpability. Political affiliation cannot substitute for proof.
This distinction becomes especially important when Malaysia confronts controversies involving institutions such as Tabung Haji, Felda, the Littoral Combat Ship programme and other episodes of alleged financial or administrative malfeasance.
Where wrongdoing occurred, it should be investigated rigorously. Where criminal liability can be established, prosecution should follow. Where administrative negligence occurred, institutional reforms should be undertaken.
But none of these propositions logically establishes the guilt of an entire political party consisting of millions of members and generations of leaders.
Umno is not one person.
Nor is Umno one administration, one faction or one historical episode.
The writer says that Umno is not one person, adding that accountability for alleged wrongdoing should be directed at specific individuals and decisions rather than applied collectively to all members. — Picture by Yusof Mat Isa
It contains reformists and conservatives, government leaders and backbenchers, veterans and younger members, federal and state politicians, as well as ordinary members who could not conceivably have known what senior officials were doing inside ministries, government-linked companies or statutory bodies.
To treat them as collectively responsible would reproduce precisely the kind of politics PH has long argued Malaysia should transcend.
There is also a constitutional principle involved. Malaysia’s criminal justice system recognises individual culpability. A person is not guilty because of association.
Political parties themselves may face legal consequences under appropriate circumstances, but the misconduct of particular office-holders cannot automatically be transferred to every member of an organisation.
The distinction between political responsibility, administrative responsibility and criminal responsibility must therefore remain clear.
Political responsibility can be broad. A government can legitimately be criticised for allowing poor governance to flourish under its watch.
Ministers can be held politically accountable for failures within their portfolios even when they did not personally commit criminal offences.
Criminal responsibility, however, requires something much more specific.
Who authorised the transaction? Who knew about it? Who benefited? Who concealed information? Who ignored professional warnings? Who exercised fiduciary responsibility? Who violated the law?
These are evidentiary questions. They cannot be answered merely by saying “Umno.”
This is why PH should be particularly careful about using overly generic language when discussing previous scandals. PH presently governs Malaysia through a coalition arrangement in which Barisan Nasional is an important partner.
If PH simultaneously depends upon Umno for governmental stability while rhetorically portraying Umno as collectively responsible for every historical controversy associated with BN governments, it creates a contradiction that will eventually become politically unsustainable.
There must instead be legal compartmentalisation.
Those who committed offences should answer for them. Those who facilitated wrongdoing should be investigated.
Those who failed in their fiduciary responsibilities should explain themselves. Those who attempted to obstruct investigations should face the appropriate consequences.
But those who were not involved must not be politically convicted through association.
Indeed, this approach can strengthen rather than weaken the campaign against corruption.
When accusations become excessively broad, the genuinely culpable can hide within the collective.
They can claim that investigations are merely partisan attacks against Umno, Malays or previous governments.
Specificity removes that defence.
A forensic approach says something very different: this is not an attack against Umno.
It is an investigation into particular decisions made by identifiable individuals under particular legal responsibilities.
That distinction is enormously important.
It also creates space for Umno itself to support institutional cleansing. Party members who had nothing to do with past misconduct should have every reason to support investigations that distinguish them from those responsible.
Indeed, Umno’s long-term rehabilitation may depend partly upon its willingness to accept such differentiation.
PH should therefore resist transforming accountability into political demonisation.
Malaysia cannot progress by replacing one form of partisan triumphalism with another.
The country needs institutions capable of distinguishing between allegation and evidence, negligence and criminality, political responsibility and legal liability.
This becomes even more important as Malaysia approaches another electoral cycle. If every controversy is converted into collective condemnation, politics becomes an endless process of mutually assured accusation.
Umno blames DAP. PAS blames DAP and PH. PH blames Umno or PN.
Each political organisation then constructs an entire community of villains.
Such politics eventually destroys the centre.
Malaysia needs the opposite: accountability without collective persecution and reconciliation without impunity.
PH therefore has an opportunity to establish a higher standard. It should insist that every credible allegation of corruption, abuse of power or institutional malfeasance be investigated thoroughly while simultaneously rejecting the proposition that membership of a political party constitutes evidence of wrongdoing.
This principle must apply equally to Umno, PKR, DAP, Amanah, Bersatu, PAS or any other political organisation.
No party should receive immunity.
But no party should be subjected to collective guilt either.
The rule of law becomes meaningful precisely when it refuses both extremes.
Malaysia does not need fewer investigations. It needs better investigations: forensic, independent, evidence-driven and directed towards those actually responsible.
Not all of Umno can possibly be guilty of every wrongdoing associated with governments in which Umno once played the dominant role.
PH should understand this distinction clearly. The objective must be to isolate wrongdoing, prosecute culpability and repair institutions – not to criminalise an entire political tradition.
That is not merely good coalition politics.
It is the essence of constitutional government.
* Phar Kim Beng is professor of Asean Studies, and director at the Institute of International and Asean Studies, International Islamic University Malaysia.
** This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.

Title: Anwar on Tabung Haji RCI findings: ‘RM12b was lost, isn’t that sakau?’
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has stressed that acts of “sakau” (siphoning of funds) did occur in Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), following the loss of billions of ringgit as highlighted in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on the institution.
The Finance Minister said the term “sakau” should not be avoided or questioned if the facts showed that money had been lost from an institution entrusted with managing the savings of Muslims.
“Some people do not like the term ‘sakau’. I want to repeat here in Melaka that there was indeed ‘sakau’ in Tabung Haji. RM12 billion was lost, isn’t that ‘sakau’? There was indeed ‘sakau’,” he said when delivering his Presidential Policy Speech at the 2026 Keadilan National Congress here today.
Anwar said action must be taken against those responsible regardless of their position or political background, as the consequences of the actions of a few individuals ultimately had to be borne by the people as a whole.
“Only some were involved in the ‘sakau’, but the ones who had to pay and bear the burden were all Malaysians, regardless of race or religion,” he said.
The Prime Minister said firmness in taking action should not be construed as political vengeance, adding that he himself would face criticism whether he acted or refrained from acting.
He said some individuals who were supposedly intelligent and highly educated appeared to be firm in fighting corruption and abuse of power, but this was merely hypocrisy because any action that did not favour those they supported would be labelled as revenge.
“Although they may appear intelligent, it is actually full of hypocrisy because when we do not take action, you say we are slow, but when we take action, you call it revenge,” Anwar said.
Meanwhile, the Prime Minister said His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim. King of Malaysia, had also decreed that efforts to uncover weaknesses in the management of institutions involving the people’s interests should not stop with TH.
He said that after the TH issue was resolved, attention would be turned to the Federal Land Consolidation and Rehabilitation Authority (Felda), in line with the government’s responsibility to ensure that people’s institutions were managed transparently and responsibly.
Anwar stressed that a more stringent enforcement process would begin now to ensure that those who committed wrongdoing were held accountable, regardless of their position, party or influence.
— Bernama

Title: Anwar announces repeal of Universities and University Colleges Act, after students push for greater freedom
Article:
AYER KEROH, Aug 15 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today announced that the government will repeal the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (UUCA), following continued calls from students for greater freedom.
Anwar, who is also PKR president, said the decision came after several amendments to the Act failed to address all concerns raised by university students, local media reported.
“University students feel that they should be free. We have given them greater freedom through amendments to the UUCA (previously), but there are still some who are dissatisfied, and they have submitted a memorandum,” he said in his policy speech at the 2026 PKR National Congress at the Melaka International Trade Centre here.
“So today, I want to announce that we will repeal the Act.”
The announcement marks a significant shift from the government’s previous approach of amending UUCA to give students greater freedom while retaining the law as the framework for public university governance.
UUCA has been amended several times since it was introduced in 1971, including changes in 2012 that allowed students to participate in political party activities outside campus.
The latest amendments, passed in 2024, included changes to student disciplinary procedures and financial management, including allowing student representative councils and student bodies to collect money and receive contributions subject to prevailing laws and regulations.
In 2023, Anwar had said sections of UUCA restricting the freedom of students and academics would be repealed, while the Higher Education Ministry said at the time that it intended to retain the Act but amend it to give students greater freedom in political activities.
The 2024 amendments also shifted disciplinary decisions involving public university students from the vice-chancellor to Student Disciplinary Committees through amendments to Section 16B.
The amendments further revised Section 15A to allow student representative councils and student bodies to raise funds and receive contributions, subject to applicable written laws and regulations.
UUCA, enacted in 1971, provides the legal framework for the governance and administration of public universities in Malaysia.
Student groups have for years called for the Act to be repealed, particularly provisions they say restrict student participation in politics and public affairs, with Anwar himself previously pledging to remove sections that limited student and academic freedom.
The government’s 2024 amendments had instead focused on improving university governance, student activities and disciplinary procedures while retaining UUCA as the governing framework.

Title: Woman rescued by public after falling from Darul Hana Bridge in Kuching
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 15 — A woman was rescued by members of the public after falling from the Darul Hana Bridge at Kuching Waterfront here yesterday evening.
Kuching district police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu confirmed the incident, saying the woman had been admitted to Sarawak General Hospital (SGH) for further treatment at the Yellow Zone of the Emergency and Trauma Unit.
“Initial investigations found that the incident was related to a personal issue — however, investigations are ongoing to determine the root cause of the incident.
“As such, the public is urged to refrain from speculating or spreading unverified information regarding the incident,” he said in a statement today.
Those with information related to the incident may contact the Kuching district police headquarters at 082-244444 or the investigating officer, Insp Logeswara, at 018-2914239.
Videos of the incident were circulated on various Facebook pages yesterday evening, showing the woman being rescued by members of the public.
Those experiencing emotional problems are encouraged to contact trained volunteers at Befrienders by calling 03-76272929 (24 hours). — Bernama

Title: Sibu latest to record unhealthy API as nine Sarawak areas affected
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 15 — Sibu is the latest area in Sarawak to record an unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) reading, bringing the total number of locations in that category to nine as of 9am today.
According to data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, Kuching recorded the highest reading at 167, followed by Samarahan (164), Serian (163), Sarikei (157), Bintulu (156), Sri Aman (154), Mukah (152), Sibu (131), and Samalaju (126).
Meanwhile, 46 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while 13 areas recorded good air quality.
API readings from 0 to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, and readings above 300 are hazardous.
API data is released hourly from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama

Title: After Tabung Haji, Anwar says King wants Felda probe next
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 15 — The government will investigate issues involving Felda after completing its probe into alleged misappropriation at Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
The move follows a directive from His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, for investigations into institutions owned by the people to go beyond TH, The Star quoted Anwar as saying at the PKR Congress in Melaka.
“The King told me last week that do not let it end with TH, (but) continue,” Anwar said in his policy speech.
Anwar said the King had specifically asked who was currently in charge of Felda, to which he replied that he was responsible for the agency.
“His Majesty also asked who is in charge of Felda now. I answered, me, (so) once TH is done, uncover what happened at Felda,” he said.
Anwar, who is also PKR president, said the government will not compromise with anyone found to have breached regulations or taken public assets.
He said the action was not to target certain parties, but to obtain certainty on the land development agency that previously carried a heavy debt burden.
“Let the enforcement agencies investigate professionally," he said.
Anwar, who is also the Pakatan Harapan chairman, said the authorities must be firm and take action, regardless of the position of the individual being investigated.
He made it clear that any action taken should not be seen as a desperate retaliatory act, but a more stringent process without any compromises.
Earlier this year, Anwar said the federal government is burdened with Felda’s debt of almost RM1 billion a year, which was allegedly due to a weak administrative management.
He said that the responsibility of paying off the financial commitment now had to be shouldered by his administration to ensure that the survival and welfare of the settlers were not affected.
Anwar said the government continues to strengthen the reform agenda to stop the practice of embezzlement, in addition to ensuring that development can be enjoyed more fairly by the people.
He said that efforts to save the country from such disruptive practices must be followed by improving the administrative system and process so that wealth is not excessively distributed to certain parties.
“In these three years, we have ensured political stability, maintained security and a growing economy.
“Now, we must continue to strengthen the reform agenda in several areas that are still pending,” he said.
